The PR changes only test-suite traits: `GLM5NextTensorParallelPagedKVTests.swift` line 19 (`@Suite(.serialized)` becomes `@Suite(.serialized, .boundedBufferCache(gib: 4))`) and `GLM5NextTensorParallelPrefixRestoreTests.swift` line 27 (adds `.boundedBufferCache`). The rest of the PagedKV test file is identical between base and head. No production code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization, key handling, or cache-storage logic is touched.

Security relevance is limited to test infrastructure. The `boundedBufferCache` trait definition is not in the supplied evidence, so its behavior is an unverified contract. I assume it only caps the MLX buffer cache for the test process. The unseen trait could change global MLX state, but that affects test execution only, not shipped provider behavior or the T-041 prefix-cache at-rest posture (HMAC names, TTL, DBK3 crypto). The prefix-restore test exercises the SSD record path under the new trait, but nothing in this diff alters the cache crypto, the TTL, or the lookup derivation.

No threat-model assets or boundaries are affected, and no threat-model update is needed. Only a minor residual question remains: the trait's implementation (outside the supplied units) should be confirmed to be test-only and not shipped in a production target.
